correctness.rationale: PASS. In the incidence poset, a graph vertex is an up beat point exactly when it has degree one; an edge with both endpoints present has a two-point incomparable lower set and is not down beat. Deleting a leaf vertex makes its unique incident edge a down beat point, so the paired deletion exactly realizes one graph leaf-pruning step. Iteration leaves the incidence poset of each cyclic component's graph 2-core and one isolated point from each tree component. The surviving 2-core vertices have degree at least two, surviving edges have two incomparable endpoints, and isolated points have no strict upper/lower set, so the result has no beat points. Stong core uniqueness gives the homotopy classification, and a poset isomorphism of nontrivial incidence components preserves minimal vertices, maximal edges and incidence, hence recovers the simple graph. The exhaustive n<=6 replay is corroborative only.
risks: The theorem is only for nonempty finite simple graphs; loops, multiedges and higher-dimensional face posets may change the beat-point analysis.

value.rationale: PASS. This is a natural complete classification for a standard graph-to-finite-space construction. It identifies a canonical, efficiently computable graph invariant exactly with the Stong core, distinguishes finite-space homotopy from weak graph homotopy, and gives an immediate decision criterion. Although the local beat-point moves are elementary, the all-graph core formula and classification are structurally reusable rather than a textbook one-line deduction.
